verdict.rationale: Codex CLI/IDE lets users add/remove MCP servers, inspect available tools before they're used, and set permission modes controlling when the agent can edit files or run commands (codex-docs-16, codex-docs-17, codex-docs-35, codex-docs-36, codex-docs-38). Org-level RBAC also exists for API/dashboard access control (codex-docs-28). However, this is largely individual/per-session configuration rather than a centralized, lead-enforced policy across a whole team, and a community post raises an open question about whether Codex still accesses sensitive filesystem data without asking (codex-comm-9), though this is not a confirmed hands-on failure. Missing for 10: team-wide/admin-enforced allowlists for tools/MCP servers, independent verification that restrictions are reliably enforced, and audit logging of tool access.
